newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Jul/Aug gas oil at minus 60cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Jul/Aug gas oil at minus 60cts.

text.p: The Singapore July/August gas oil swaps time spread has widened further on high prompt physical stocks and a perception that demand will pick up in August, traders said.
"The July/August spread is widening because of the prompt physical overhang and market expectations that demand will improve in August," one trader said.
July paper was last quoted steady from late Tuesday at $22.25/$22.35 per barrel, brokers said. The market traded early in the day at $22.35 before easing slightly at midday, they said.
Similiar movements was seen for August which traded earlier at $22.95 before edging down to $22.85/$22.95, brokers said.
The improved sentiment for August which was actively traded on Tuesday had led to a widening of the time spread to value at around minus 60 cents, brokers said.

The July/August spread was last quoted at minus 65 to minus 55 cents, they said. The spread traded early Tuesday at minus 35 cents, compared to late last week's minus 25 cents traded level, brokers said.
Traders said the firmer August prices were due to expectations that the prompt overhang would clear by then as the big buyers such as China, India and Indonesia return to the market.

Early signs of better buying were seen with India issuing two term tenders to purchase 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 percent sulphur diesel for August 1997 to March 1998 delivery, on top of the 3.2 million tonnes it had already bought on a one-year term basis for June 1997 to May 1998 delivery.
Traders said despite the issue of a second term tender, Indian monthly spot imports are not likely to be affected due to high domestic demand.
Indonesian July and August purchases are expected to increase due to shutdown of crude units at Balikpapan and Cilacap for maintenance.
Chinese buying was also anticipated because China had cut back its second quarter demand considerably due to high purchases of just over 2 million tonnes in the first quarter.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade as widened sharply with July last quoted at $0.90/$1.10 per barrel due to the weak gas oil prices.
Fuel oil swaps were steady with July last quoted at $100.00/$101.00, brokers said.
